text:
Posted by John. R. Edwardson on Mar 14th, 2018 // No Comments 
Finisar (NASDAQ: FNSR) recently received a number of ratings updates from brokerages and research firms: 3/10/2018 – Finisar was given a new $23.00 price target on by analysts at Barclays PLC. They now have a “hold” rating on the stock. 3/9/2018 – Finisar was given a new $15.00 price target on by analysts at Goldman Sachs Group Inc. They now have a “sell” rating on the stock. 3/9/2018 – Finisar was downgraded by analysts at Needham & Company LLC from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating. They now have a $29.41 price target on the stock, up previously from $16.64. 3/9/2018 – Finisar is now covered by analysts at Morgan Stanley. They set an “equal weight” rating and a $21.00 price target on the stock. 3/9/2018 – Finisar had its “buy” rating reaffirmed by analysts at DA Davidson. They now have a $22.00 price target on the stock, down previously from $24.00. 3/9/2018 – Finisar had its “buy” rating reaffirmed by analysts at B. Riley. They now have a $17.50 price target on the stock, down previously from $18.00. 3/9/2018 – Finisar had its price target lowered by analysts at Stifel Nicolaus from $24.00 to $22.00. They now have a “buy” rating on the stock. 3/7/2018 – Finisar was upgraded by analysts at BidaskClub from a “strong sell” rating to a “sell” rating. 3/5/2018 – Finisar had its “outperform” rating reaffirmed by analysts at Raymond James Financial, Inc.. 3/5/2018 – Finisar was downgraded by analysts at UBS Group AG from a “strong-buy” rating to an “outperform” rating. 3/5/2018 – Finisar had its “buy” rating reaffirmed by analysts at William Blair. They wrote, “We expect the company to come in roughly in line on revenue with a downward bias to EPS due to ongoing datacom pricing pressure affecting gross margin. The Street is looking for $333 million on revenue (roughly flat sequentially) and $0.23 for EPS; we are in line on revenue and a penny below consensus on EPS. We believe the company could see modest quarter-over-quarter expansion in 3-D sensing (revenue is relatively small to be affected by recent Apple [AAPL $176.21; Not Rated] iPhoneX cuts) offsetting ongoing inventory correction in China (at Huawei and ZTE) and product transition at hyperscale customers (Amazon [AMZN $1,500.25; Outperform] transitioning from 40G to 100G). The biggest risk to Finisar remains gross margins, which could remain pressured until datacom pricing stabilizes, cost reduction products become available, and/or higher-margin products (CFP2-ACO and ROADMs) begin to ship in volume.”” 3/1/2018 – Finisar had its price target lowered by analysts at B. Riley from $20.00 to $18.00. They now have a “buy” rating on the stock. 2/26/2018 – Finisar had its price target lowered by analysts at Loop Capital from $19.00 to $17.00. They now have a “hold” rating on the stock. 2/8/2018 – Finisar was upgraded by analysts at Zacks Investment Research from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating. According to Zacks, “FINISAR CORP. is a provider of fiber optic subsystems and network test and monitoring systems which enable high-speed data communications over local area networks, or LANs, storage area networks, or SANs, and metropolitan access networks, or MANs. They are focused on the application of digital fiber optics to provide aline of high-performance, reliable, value-added optical subsystems for data networking and storage equipment manufacturers. “ 2/2/2018 –Finisar was downgraded by analysts at ValuEngine from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating. 1/29/2018 – Finisar was downgraded by analysts at Piper Jaffray Companies from an “overweight” rating to a “neutral” rating. 1/29/2018 – Finisar is now covered by analysts at Loop Capital. They set a “hold” rating and a $19.00 price target on the stock. 1/25/2018 – Finisar was upgraded by analysts at ValuEngine from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating. 1/24/2018 – Finisar had its price target lowered by analysts at Stifel Nicolaus from $26.00 to $24.00. They now have a “buy” rating on the stock. 1/15/2018 – Finisar was downgraded by analysts at Goldman Sachs Group Inc from a “neutral” rating to a “sell” rating. They now have a $16.00 price target on the stock, down previously from $22.74. 
Finisar Co. ( NASDAQ FNSR ) opened at $19.93 on Wednesday. Finisar Co. has a 1-year low of $16.64 and a 1-year high of $29.07. The company has a current ratio of 4.06, a quick ratio of 3.24 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.29. The stock has a market capitalization of $2,270.00, a price-to-earnings ratio of 16.20, a P/E/G ratio of 2.11 and a beta of 1.02. Get Finisar Co alerts: 
Finisar (NASDAQ:FNSR) last posted its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, March 8th. The technology company reported $0.20 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, missing the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $0.23 by ($0.03). Finisar had a net margin of 7.35% and a return on equity of 5.97%. The business had revenue of $332.40 million for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $333.15 million. During the same quarter in the previous year, the firm earned $0.59 EPS. Finisar’s revenue was down 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. equities analysts expect that Finisar Co. will post 0.65 earnings per share for the current year. In other Finisar news, Director Jerry S. Rawls sold 30,209 shares of Finisar stock in a transaction on Thursday, February 1st. The stock was sold at an average price of $17.94, for a total transaction of $541,949.46. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through the SEC website . Also, SVP Mark Colyar sold 1,692 shares of Finisar stock in a transaction on Monday, December 18th. The shares were sold at an average price of $22.15, for a total value of $37,477.80. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last 90 days, insiders have sold 56,392 shares of company stock valued at $1,119,833. 1.02% of the stock is owned by company insiders. 
Finisar Corporation (Finisar) is a provider of optical subsystems and components that are used in data communication and telecommunication applications. The Company’s optical subsystems consist of transmitters, receivers, transceivers, transponders and active optical cables, which provide the fundamental optical-electrical or optoelectronic interface for interconnecting the electronic equipment used in these networks, including the switches, routers, and servers used in wireline networks.
